builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents
summary: MADS replaces hand-collected or purely cooperative dialogue corpora with a multi-agent simulation pipeline that injects adversarial user behavior, plus an associated benchmark (six domains, 55 personas, 1095 conversations, ~66% failure-prone trajectories) for training and evaluating tool-calling agents. The cost is the generation and validation compute (feasible via third-party LLM APIs on a constrained budget), pipeline engineering effort, and a two-stage SFT-plus-RLVR training regime that itself requires non-trivial infrastructure if replicated. What can fail: simulated adversarial personas may not match real user distributions, the abstract reports no quantified robustness improvement over baselines, and RLVR on a single 24 GB GPU is practical only for small models, so gains may not transfer to the reader's deployment scale.
rationale: The pipeline is API-feasible and directly relevant to production tool-calling agents, but the absence of quantified robustness gains and the unvalidated realism of synthetic adversarial trajectories require workload-specific testing before adoption.
technique: Multi-agent adversarial dialogue simulation for robustness training
